Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. _tL-- FEB 2 R 2025 MR. ROBERT OROZCO tvorozco@yahoo.com Dear Mr. Orozco: This refers to your email dated 13 September 2024 seeking legal advice on a matter concerning the hereinbelow issue: I would like to inquire or seek an opinion from your office if it's legal to have the name of a senator permanently and prominently displayed on the facade of the newly built Barangay Halls. Thank you very much in advance. Foremost, your letter did not provide sufficient details surrounding your concern in order for us to formulate a responsive opinion on the matter. It would require us to make assumptions about the issue, not apparent in your query. As such, we will only provide a relevant academic discussion. We refer you to Section 19 of Republic Act No. 11975 or the General Appropriations Act for Fiscal Year 2024, which provides: Sec. 19. Prohibition on the Display and/or Affixture of the Name, Image and Likeness of Public Officials on Government Projects. The display and/or affixture of the name, picture, image motto, logo, color, motif, initials, or other symbol or graphical representation associated with any public official, whether elected or appointed, on signboards for all programs, activities, and projects funded under this Act shall be considered as unnecessary pursuant to COA Circular No. 2013- 004 dated January 30, 2013, as amended, and therefore prohibited. The foregoing prohibition is likewise found in Section 19 of Republic Act No. 12116, or the General Appropriations Act for Fiscal Year 2025. The prohibition essentially means that government officials are not allowed to have their names, pictures, or any other recognizable representation displayed on government-funded projects or signage, effectively preventing them from using public projects for self-promotion. We hope this sheds light on the issue. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54
